entry.title: Can Open Source Make AI Agents Safer?

media:group.media:title: Can Open Source Make AI Agents Safer?
media:group.media:description:
Hugging Face co-founder Thomas Wolf and ServiceNow’s Amanda Grady, SVP of AI Platform Security, join the NVIDIA AI Podcast to explain how to keep AI agents safe when telling a model “please don’t” is no longer enough.
They cover why firm boundaries beat persuadable models, what happened when Hugging Face was attacked by a swarm of AI agents, and why security is what lets companies put agents to real work. This is the 15-minute best-moments edit. The full-length episode is on your favorite podcast platform!
In this episode: 0:16 Why guardrails inside the model aren’t enough 2:00 The attack on Hugging Face, and why open models mattered 3:28 Agent identity and the AI Passport 6:03 Security as an unlocker for AI 8:33 Why open source is more secure, not less 10:59 Physical AI and the micro-duck 13:12 Fine-tuning for everyone 14:11 Who gets to build AI
Guests Thomas Wolf, Co-founder, Hugging Face Amanda Grady, SVP, AI Platform Security, ServiceNow
Follow on Spotify: https://open.spotify.com/show/4TB4pnynaiZ6YHoKmyVN0L Follow on Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/nvidia-ai-podcast/id1186480811 Learn more: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/ai-security-agent-stack/

entry.title: NVIDIA cuPhoton Brings Real-Time Black Hole Science to GPUs

media:group.media:title: NVIDIA cuPhoton Brings Real-Time Black Hole Science to GPUs
media:group.media:description:
NVIDIA cuPhoton moves the scientific data pipeline onto GPUs, helping researchers study black holes as events unfold.
- Eight radio observatories worked together as a virtual telescope the size of Earth to capture the first image of a black hole in the M87 galaxy - cuPhoton streams only the data needed for black hole jets and overlaps loading with signal processing, reconstruction, analysis and visualization, all of which AI agents can run - It speeds up data loading by up to 3,700x and correlation by up to 460x, scaling across multi-node systems powered by the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform - Data can now be acquired at rates up to 345 GHz, cuPhoton reduces months of compute to minutes and help resolve the light rings around black hole
Learn More: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/high-performance-computing/ai-for-science/cuphoton/

entry.title: Real-Time Discovery Starts With NVIDIA DAQIRI

media:group.media:title: Real-Time Discovery Starts With NVIDIA DAQIRI
media:group.media:description:
Every discovery begins with a signal. NVIDIA DAQIRI connects high-bandwidth instrument data to accelerated computing, so AI can process live sensor streams while an experiment or industrial process is still underway.
Instead of capturing data, writing it to disk, and analyzing it later, workflows can sense, reason, and respond in real time.
- Streams hundreds to thousands of gigabits of instrument data per second into GPU memory - Berkeley Lab’s Molecular Foundry uses DAQIRI to stream over 500 Gb/s from a new camera, delivering results during the experiment - Enables live scan analysis, telescope signal characterization, experiment guidance, and synchronized interactive digital twins
Learn More: https://developer.nvidia.com/daqiri

entry.title: 20 Years of CUDA: Honoring the Architects of Progress

media:group.media:title: 20 Years of CUDA: Honoring the Architects of Progress
media:group.media:description:
For 20 years, pioneers, researchers, developers, and creators have changed the world with CUDA.
NVIDIA announced CUDA in 2006 as a different way to compute - giving developers direct access to the parallel power of the GPU.
Two decades later, the CUDA platform is enabling work in scientific computing, professional visualization, autonomous vehicles, drug discovery and healthcare, generative AI, robotics and more.
Today, more than 11 million developers are leveraging CUDA for their work and a new generation of students, researchers and builders continue to shape the future. We’re celebrating 20 years of CUDA and honoring the architects of progress.

entry.title: Meet the Startup: Aegiq, A Full-Stack Photonic Quantum Computing Company

media:group.media:title: Meet the Startup: Aegiq, A Full-Stack Photonic Quantum Computing Company
media:group.media:description:
Quantum computers have a deployment problem. Aegiq is solving it.
The Sheffield-based startup is building photonic quantum computers designed to connect over standard fiber networks and manufacture using standard semiconductor processes — making quantum hardware practical to deploy at scale, not just in a lab.
In this interview, Aegiq’s team walks through how they’ve integrated NVIDIA technology into their core workflow. Using NVIDIA’s Ising solver, they cut quantum dot calibration time by 3x. With cuTENSOR libraries, they went from 1 million point meshes on existing GPUs to billions — and are targeting 10 trillion point meshes in collaboration with NVIDIA. The applications are real and near-term: aerospace simulation, fusion energy, materials science, quantum chemistry.
Aegiq joined NVIDIA Inception to accelerate access to customers and compute, and is now one of the startups demonstrating what happens when photonic quantum hardware meets GPU-accelerated simulation.
🌱 Aegiq is a member of NVIDIA Inception, a program supporting startups building at the frontier of AI and deep tech.
Learn more about NVIDIA Inception: https://nvda.ws/4kjJM2n.
